#### Validations Tab

On this tab, you can manually set or edit validation parameters for a meter. If the Run on Imports and Edits option is set to "Yes", validations will be performed during imports and edits. If this option set to "No", validations will not be performed.

If a value is out of validation range, an exception will be generated. All exceptions generated can be viewed and edited within the Exception Resolver. Exceptions will only be generated the Run on Imports and Edits option is set to "Yes" and the item has a value to check against.

You can also use validations to track the data in the Max Exception Severity column in the Final Form (rollups) tables. By setting the severity of any exceptions to an elevated level, custom exports or other downstream systems can examine the Max Exception Severity value to determine if a record is ready to be exported.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Flowing Parameters">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Flowing Parameters Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Flowing Parameters">

#### General

Flowing Parameters validations allow for definition of minimum and maximum limits on Flow Variable (DP or Pulses), Static Pressure, Temperature, Volume, Energy NSV, Mass, Flow Basis (Extension, Raw Volume), Volume Correlation Factor (VCF), Speed of Sound and Flow Time variables.

If a liquid meter uses a volumetric measurement, then net standard volume can be validated; otherwise, mass can be validated.

For gas meters only, when the system option is enabled, high-high and low-low limits are available for additional flowing parameter validations, which generate associated exceptions.

When high-high/low-low limits are available in addition to high/low limits, only one exception is generated for data that exceeds the set limits. For example: If a value exceeds both the high limit and the high-high limit, only one exception will be generated for exceeding the high-high limit. A second exception for exceeding the High limit will not be generated.

- **Run on Imports and Edits** - When set to "Yes", Flowing Parameter validations are enabled for the meter.
- **Extension** - The extension reported by the meter, or, if FLOWCAL calculates the extension, the average flowing extension (orifice meters only).
- **Raw Volume** - The actual volume, which does not have the temperature, pressure, or compressibility corrections required for standard volume (AGA-7 meters only).
- **VCF** - The volume calculated by the electronic flow meter, divided by the FLOWCAL-calculated volume (gas meters only).

This factor is typically close to 1 (example: .997) because of differences between the two sets of volumes. In some cases, such as intermittent flow, these differences can exceed 20%. These differences occur when significant fluctuations of the flowing parameters (DP, P, or T) happen within the record.

- **Correlation Factor** - The Mass, GSV, NSV, IV, and SWV calculated by the electronic flow meter the user is editing, divided by the FLOWCAL calculated number for each value (liquid meters only).

This factor is typically close to 1 (example: .997), because there will usually be small differences between the two sets of values. The same Min and Max limits are applied to all five Liquid Correlation Factors for Mass, GSV, NSV, IV, and SWV.

- **Speed of Sound** - Only applicable to ultrasonic meters that import speed of sound diagnostics.

- **Max Deviation** - The difference between the meter's imported raw volume and the volume FLOWCAL calculates from the pipe length and pipe diameter (line pack calculations only).

  The comparison can determine a unit difference or a percent difference.

  - For a unit difference test, the calculated value must be within the raw volume +/- the deviation amount. If the calculated value is outside of this range, exception 1050 will be generated.
    <div class="example">

    <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Max Dev1">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

    Raw volume = 10,000, unit difference = 100. The calculated volume must be within the range of 9,900 to 10,100.

    </div>
  - For a percent difference test, the calculated value must be within the raw volume +/- the deviation percentage. If the calculated value is outside of this range, exception 1048 will be generated
    <div class="example">

    <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Max Dev2">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

    Raw volume = 10,000, percent deviation = 2. The calculated volume must be within the range of 9,800 to 10,200.

    </div>

- **Flow Time** - Comparison of the meter's real flow time to the set minimum and maximum values. Options are Minutes, Hours, Days, % of an hour, or No Entry/Clear. If the flow time is outside of the range specified here, an exception is generated.

  The No Entry/Clear option deletes any previously entered value. Setting the value to 0 will not disable the validation; it will set the minimum value to 0.

  If the “% of an hour” option is selected in the drop-down, values shown will display with a decimal precision of two places.

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Flow Time">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  If the previous drop-down value selected was Days (DD HHH:MM:SS) and the validation value was 00 000:45:25 = 2725 s = 75.694444444444 %, the Meter Editor will display 75.69 % if the drop-down is changed to “% of an hour”.

  </div>

  For a daily resolution meter, it may be easier to enter and read validation limits in hours (23:55:00 and 24:05:00) rather than seconds (85100 and 86700). Even for hourly resolution, minutes (59 and 61) may be easier to interpret than seconds (3540 and 3660).

- **Skip No-Flow Exceptions** - When set to "Yes", an exception will not be generated when a meter has a record that is zero flow, even if the parameter is outside of the validation limits.

  For orifice meters, no flow is defined as:

  - Volume = 0 and differential pressure \< no flow cutoff; or
  - Volume = 0, differential pressure not given and flow time = 0; or
  - Volume = 0, differential pressure not given, and flow time not given

  For non-orifice meters, no flow is defined as:

  - Volume = 0 and flow time = 0; or
  - Volume = 0 and pulses = 0

- **Scale for Flow Time** - If enabled, the data for accumulated fields (volume, energy, pulses, and mass) will be scaled based on flow time.

#### Coriolis

- **Drive Gain Min / Max** - Minimum and maximum allowed drive gain values (Coriolis meters only).

#### Ultrasonic 2

Ultrasonic flow meters measure the travel time difference of ultrasonic sound waves transmitted with and against the fluid flow direction. The time difference, along with the physical configuration of the meter, is used to determine the average velocity of the flow.

Speed of Sound Validation

When the speed of sound differs across records (i.e., over time) more than the limit configured here, [exception 2501](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2500-2599.md) is generated.

- **Duration (Hours)** - The number of previous UFM diagnostics records that the current record is to be validated against.
- **Percent Difference Allowed** - The maximum percentage of difference allowed between the current record and the previous records.

When the speed of sound variance exceeds the limit configured here, [exception 2502](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2500-2599.md) is generated.

- **Variance** - Amount of variance allowed between FLOWCAL's speed of sound calculation and the value imported.
- **Compare Using** - When performing the variance validation for speed of sound, the variance can be specified as a unit difference or a percent difference.

Flow Velocity Profile Validation

- **Baseline** - A user-defined target value for the calculated profile.
- **Percent Difference Allowed** - A comparison between the profile baseline and the calculated baseline. This value is the maximum percentage of variance allowed before [exception 2503](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2500-2599.md) is generated.
  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Profile Pct Diff">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Profile Pct Diff">

  | Calculated Profile From UFM Periodic Data | Baseline | Pct. Difference Allowed | Percent Difference Calculated/Baseline | Exception Generated |
  |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
  | 5.02 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((5.02/5.095)-1)\*100=1.472% | No |
  | 6 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((6/5.095)-1)\*100=17.763% | Yes |
  | 4 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((4/5.095)-1)\*100=21.492% | Yes |

   

  </div>

  </div>

Flow Velocity Symmetry Validation

- **Baseline** - A user-defined target value for the calculated symmetry.
- **Percent Difference Allowed** - A comparison between the symmetry baseline and the calculated baseline. This value is the maximum percentage of variance allowed before [exception 2504](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2500-2599.md) is generated.
  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Symmetry Pct Diff">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /> Example</a>

  <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Symmetry Pct Diff">

  | Calculated Symmetry From UFM Periodic Data | Baseline | Pct. Difference Allowed | Percent Difference Calculated/Baseline | Exception Generated |
  |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
  | 1.001 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((1.001/1.0001)-1)\*100=0.089% | No |
  | 0.9 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((0.9/1.0001)-1)\*100=-10.009% | Yes |
  | 1.1 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((1.1/1.0001)-1)\*100=9.989% | Yes |

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Analysis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Analysis Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Analysis">

Analysis validations assess analysis data applied to a meter. Much like the flowing parameters, minimum and maximum values can be specified for each of the components available under the **Mole %** button.

- **Quality button** - Quality-related information such as total GPM, relative density, heating value, sample pressure, and sample temperature can be validated. Available for gas meters only
- **Mole % button** - Mole % validations are available for both gas and liquid meters.
- **Liquids button** - Liquids validations are available for liquid meters only.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Frozen Values">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Frozen Values Sub-Tab</a>\*

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Frozen Values">

Frozen Values validations are used if a meter continues to report the same value for a data point over several consecutive records. It is possible the reading is inaccurate, and the results are caused by a frozen value that is not being updated.

In this section, you can specify whether to look for frozen values, the duration for which each value must persist before it is considered frozen, and the deadband for each value, which serves as a tolerance level within which values will be treated as identical.

To specify a deadband value of 0, set the value to a very small number (for example, 0.001) rather than 0. Specifying 0 will not trigger validation for that data point.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Single Run">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Single Run Sub-Tab</a>\*

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Single Run">

Single Run validations enable user-defined comparisons of a meter’s current record to prior records to identify excessive variation. For each flowing parameter, you can specify whether to compare the data to the previous record or to the previous day.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Multi Run">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Multiple Run Sub-Tab</a>\*

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Multi Run">

Multiple Run validations are similar to Single Run validations, but you can also compare the meter’s record with up to four other meter records. This feature provides a comparison for multi-tube locations, check meters versus sales meters, or upstream and downstream comparisons.

- **Temperature Differentiation** - This is useful if two meters have the same feed and one of them is shut in. Where the meter is shut in, the temperature should not track the temperature of the line with flow. If it does track, that indicates a leak. In this case, FLOWCAL will generate an exception to try to identify the problem.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Expert Systems">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Expert Systems Sub-Tab</a>\*

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Expert Systems">

Expert Systems validations apply statistical analyses to historical data to identify uncharacteristic changes in a meter's data flow pattern. If the value in the current record being imported is outside the range of the lower and upper bounds, which are calculated using a running or weighted average (Average Count field), an exception is generated.

The following options are available on the Expert Systems sub-tab:

- **Average Method** - The method by which average values will be calculated.
  - **Running** - A straight average of all values where each value has an equal weighting.

    <br/>![](data:image/png;base64,)

  - **Weighted** - Each value to be averaged is assigned a weight. The oldest record is assigned a weight of 1. Newer records carry more weight, increasing by an interval of 1.

    <br/>![](data:image/png;base64,)

- **Average Count** - The number of records used to calculate the average; this count starts with the record immediately prior to the record being validated and goes back in time.

  Missing data is included in the average count, but it is not included in the average calculation. A data point with no value in an existing value does get included in the average calculation.

  If all records in the period to be used for average calculation are missing, no validation takes place for the current iteration. The validation process moves on to the next record to be validated.

- **Exclude E/S Exception** - If set to "Yes", data points with Expert Systems exceptions are excluded during the validation process. When an Expert System exception has been flagged, it is a data anomaly, which may not be desirable when calculating averages for more data points for the same meter.
  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Exclude ES">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /> Example</a>

  <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Exclude ES">

  | Effective Date      | Volume | Exception |
  |:--------------------|:------:|:---------:|
  | 1/1/2017 07:00:00   |  1290  |    \-     |
  | 1/1/2017 08:00:00   |  1200  |    \-     |
  | 1/1/2017 09:00:00   |  800   |   2236    |
  | 1/1/2017 10:00:00   |  1250  |    \-     |
  | 1/1/2017 11:00:00   |  1260  |    \-     |
  | 1/1/2017 12:00:00   |  1290  |    \-     |
  | 1/1/2017 13:00:00\* |  1350  |    \-     |

  \* Record being validated

  The record at 1/1/2017 13:00:00 is being validated, with an average count of 5. Typically, this would mean that the average would be calculated from the previous five records (1/1/2017 8:00:00 through 1/1/2017 12:00:00).

  However, note that the 1/1/2017 9:00:00 record has a validation exception (2236 ES - Volume failed). This exception is an expert systems validation, so this record is excluded from the process. The average is then calculated from the other four records: (1200+1250+1260+1290) / 4 = 1250.

  </div>

  </div>

- **Step** - The number of consecutive records to be validated using the calculated average. Valid inputs are integers between 1 and 96. If a step value is not provided, the value will default to 1. The first step of a contract month will always start on the first period of the month. If a step spans two months, the validation process will start over at the beginning of the second month.
  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Step">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" /> Example</a>

  

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 403;height: 136;" />

  </div>

- **Method**
  - **Percent Difference**

    Lower Bound = Average - (Percent Difference \* Average)

    Upper Bound = Average + (Percent Difference \* Average)

  - **Std Deviation**

    Lower Bound = Average - (ES Limit \* Standard Deviation)

    Upper Bound = Average + (ES Limit \* Standard Deviation)

- **LO Limit / HI Limit** - When the Expert Systems calculation is complete, FLOWCAL validates if any data points were below or above the low and high benchmark limits. An exception is generated for any data points outside of the set limits.

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Expert Sys">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Expert Systems Example</a>

  <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Expert Sys">

  | Step |  Effective Date   | Volume | Average Used for Validation |
  |:----:|:-----------------:|:------:|:---------------------------:|
  |  \-  | 1/1/2017 04:00:00 |  1290  |             \-              |
  |  \-  | 1/1/2017 05:00:00 |  1200  |             \-              |
  |  \-  | 1/1/2017 06:00:00 |  1130  |             \-              |
  |  \-  | 1/1/2017 07:00:00 |  1250  |             \-              |
  |  \-  | 1/1/2017 08:00:00 |  1260  |             \-              |
  |  1   | 1/1/2017 09:00:00 |  1290  |            1210             |
  |  1   | 1/1/2017 10:00:00 |  1350  |            1210             |
  |  1   | 1/1/2017 11:00:00 |  1340  |            1210             |
  |  2   | 1/1/2017 12:00:00 |  1370  |            1310             |
  |  2   | 1/1/2017 13:00:00 |  1310  |            1310             |
  |  2   | 1/1/2017 14:00:00 |  1315  |            1310             |

  In this example, the average count value is 4 and step value is 3. The contract day is 1 and contract hour is 9.

  For validation of January data, the 1/1/2017 9:00:00 record is validated first. Since the step value is 3, the three records starting at 1/1/2017 9:00:00 are validated using the same average. The average is calculated from the four previous records starting with the record immediately before the beginning of the step and going back in time. This means the average of the four records starting with 1/1/2017 8:00:00 and going back in time will be used: (1200+1130+1250+1260) / 4 = 1210

  The next step begins with the record after the first step (1/1/2017 12:00:00). The three records starting at 1/1/2017 12:00:00 are validated using the average calculated from the four preceding records from 1/1/2017 8:00:00 to 1/1/2017 11:00:00: (1260+1290+1350+1340) / 4 = 1310

  </div>

  </div>

   

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Expert Sys Missing Data">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Expert Systems Example With Missing Data</a>

  <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Expert Sys Missing Data">

  |   Effective Date    | Temperature | Volume | Weight |
  |:-------------------:|:-----------:|:------:|:------:|
  |  1/1/2017 07:00:00  |     71      |  1100  |        |
  |  1/1/2017 08:00:00  |     79      |  1200  |   1    |
  |  1/1/2017 09:00:00  |             |  800   |   2    |
  |     \[missing\]     |             |        |        |
  |     \[missing\]     |             |        |        |
  |  1/1/2017 12:00:00  |     85      |  1300  |   3    |
  | 1/1/2017 13:00:00\* |     86      |  1350  |        |

  \* Record being validated

  **Running average of volume** - To validate volume of the 1/1/2017 13:00:00 record, records in the five-hour period of 1/1/2017 8:00:00 – 1/1/2017 12:00:00 are averaged. As two hours in the period are missing data, the average is calculated as (1200+800+1300) / 3 = 1100.

  **Weighted average of volume** - The oldest record in the period, 1/1/2017 8:00:00, is assigned with the weight of 1. Weight increases by 1 for each record with data until the record immediately before the record being validated. The two hours missing data are not included in the average calculation, and are not assigned a weight.

  **Temperature validation** - The 1/1/2017 9:00:00 record does not have a temperature value. The running average of temperature would be calculated as (79+85) / 2 = 83.

  </div>

  </div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Final Form">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Final Form Sub-Tab</a>\*

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Final Form">

Final Form occurs on rolled-up data at hourly, daily, or monthly resolution. Min/Max and Expert Systems validations are available for Final Form.

You can flag daily and monthly values comparable to nominations for the day or month. Editing the daily and/or monthly validation ranges routinely will help you identify the in-line comparison to the marketing nominations set at the beginning of each day and/or month. This tab is also useful when trying to maintain contractual agreements between two parties.

The Max monthly final form meter data validation is performed when data changes even if the month is not complete. Exceptions for high monthly values are generated as soon as a given monthly value exceeds the max validation set point even when the month is not yet complete. Validations for Min values are checked only when the month is complete.

#### Min/Max

Click the **Min/Max** button to access the following options:

- **DE Alarm Count** - Used strictly for a specific field unit named Total Flow. This allows the user to set values that will indicate the Differential Error limit expected to see on a daily basis.
- **Back Flow Percentage** - Used strictly for a specific field unit named Total Flow. Setting the Back Flow Percentage limit, the user will be able to flag when to receive an exception on typical back flow of the field unit.

</div>

<span id="MeterFactorKFactor"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="MF-KF">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />MF/KF Sub-Tab</a>\*

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="MF-KF">

Meter factor and K-factor (MF/KF) validations provide a comparison of a meter characteristic value to a range from an established baseline value. See Unit Diff and % Diff below to determine the range.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 586;height: 545;" />

The following items are available on the MF/KF sub-tab:

- **Baseline Enable** - Enter "Yes" to enable baseline factor validations.

- **Product grid** - Displays the baseline details of each configured product

- **Select Product** - If the [Validate Products](Liquids%20Tab.md#ValidateProducts) option is enabled in the Meter Editor, this product selector will contain the meter's valid products; otherwise, it will contain the complete list of products.

- **Baseline Date** - The date this baseline information was established. This is an informational value.

  The characteristic will be validated against the current baseline factors without regard to the baseline date.

- **Meter Factor** - The user-determined baseline meter factor.

- **K Factor** - The user-determined baseline K-factor.

- **Unit Diff** - The scalar amount added to or subtracted from the baseline factor to determine an acceptable range.
  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Unit Diff">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  The acceptable range for a characteristic meter factor is between (Meter Factor - Unit Diff) and (Meter Factor + Unit Diff).

  </div>

- **% Diff** - The percent amount applied to the baseline factor to determine an acceptable range.
  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Pct Diff">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  The acceptable range for a characteristic K-factor is between (K-Factor \* (1 + (% Diff/100) ) ) and (K Factor \* (1 - (% Diff/100) ) ).

  </div>

The initial set up screen provides a General product. This baseline will apply to all products for which a specific validation has not been added. The General product cannot be removed.

Values that are not configured will not cause an exception. It is not necessary to provide both a meter factor and a K-factor, or to provide both a value for Unit Diff and % Diff. If a product row is added and no other values are provided for it, no validation will take place for that product.

See: [MKF Exceptions 2451 - 2454](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2400-2499.md)

</div>

 

**\*** Not available for dead oil meters or flash gas meters.

 

#### See also:

- [Run Validations](../../Tools/Toolbox/Run%20Validations.md)

</div>
